chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a sick man who divorces his wife in that state. He said: “No. But he may marry if he wishes. If he consummates the marriage with her, she inherits from him; and if he does not consummate the marriage with her, then his marriage is invalid.”

key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person whose legal capacity in this context is being discussed
key_terms.نِكَاحُهُ: his marriage contract or marital union
key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجَ: to marry; to contract a marriage
key_terms.يُطَلِّقُ: divorces; pronounces divorce upon his wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sick man divorcing or marrying during his illness, and does the new wife inherit?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the marital actions of a sick man in the state of illness associated with death. It distinguishes between divorce and remarriage, and states that inheritance and validity of the later marriage are tied to consummation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4876 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbub narrated from Ibn Bukayr from ʿUbayd ibn Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a sick man who divorces his wife in that state (of illness).
Imam (as) said: "No, but he may marry if he wishes. If he consummates the marriage, she will inherit from him. However, if he does not consummate the marriage, then his marriage is invalid."
